//: Rules used to identify and explain sensitive fields in uploaded OpenAPI/Swagger schemas. keyTerms match field paths; valuePatterns match example/default/enum values.

rules.label: Credential or Secret
rules.why: Credentials and session material can allow account takeover or unauthorized API access if exposed, logged, replayed, or returned unnecessarily.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm values are never returned unnecessarily, are redacted from logs, transported only over TLS, rotated when exposed, and stored hashed or encrypted as appropriate.

rules.label: Personal Data
rules.why: Personal data can identify or contact an individual and may be subject to privacy, retention, and access-control requirements.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm collection is necessary, access is limited, logs and exports are minimized, and masking or retention controls are in place where appropriate.

rules.label: Social Security Number
rules.why: Social Security Numbers are high-risk government identifiers that can enable identity theft if exposed.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm collection is strictly necessary, values are encrypted at rest, masked in UI/logs, never used as public identifiers, and access is tightly controlled.

rules.label: Payment Card Data
rules.why: Payment card data can bring PCI obligations and can be used for fraud if exposed.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm card data is tokenized where possible, CVV is never stored, logs are redacted, and PCI-scoped systems and access are clearly controlled.

rules.label: Financial Account Data
rules.why: Financial account identifiers can enable fraud, account correlation, or unauthorized payment activity.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm values are encrypted, masked in logs/UI, access is audited, and only required systems can retrieve full values.

rules.label: Health Data
rules.why: Health data may be regulated and can reveal sensitive medical information about an individual.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm minimum necessary use, strict access controls, audit logging, encryption, and retention requirements.

rules.label: Tenant or Resource Identifier
rules.why: Tenant and resource identifiers can become IDOR pivots if authorization does not bind the requested ID to the authenticated principal.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm identifiers are opaque or non-enumerable, authorization is enforced server-side for every ID, and cross-tenant access attempts are logged.
